sessions.title: Q5 A different job, not better features
sessions.oneLine: Build the wall of sheets A to E from public facts only, then write the one job, the comparison set and the claims table.
sessions.purpose: Turn "a million times better" into one job for one customer, using only what is public about Duel: what Duel demonstrably offers; what its customers value or struggle with, with evidence; where Sway could be meaningfully different; why someone would switch, use Sway alongside, or adopt it first; and what might be hard to copy. The question: what job does Sway do that a brand-owned programme cannot, for whom? Blake abstains on non-public Duel content and the abstention is logged.
inputs: The Duel fact sheet, eight public rows printed as cut-out slips on Thu 8 Oct, each with its source URL and evidence label

steps.text: Swap and read the memos and replies; cross out any reply line that relies on a feature outside the MVP boundary. Blake writes nothing about Duel and Tori logs the abstention (D1-04-abstain).

Sheet A, what Duel demonstrably offers: Tori sticks the pre-printed fact-sheet slips that match her own screenshots. Nothing else enters A; a row she cannot match to a screenshot is struck; Blake reads only.

Sheet B, what customers value or struggle with: one note per item from the Duel evidence sheet and the commercial prep pack, each with a URL and a label. No brand conversation happened before the workshop, so founder-held items are [FOUNDER ASSERTION].

Sheet C, where Sway could be meaningfully different: two minutes alone, then merge. Every note names the customer and the advantage type (outcomes, experience, speed, economics or capability). Candidates: who can be an advocate; where recommendation is observed; who pays first; who owns the record. Anything Duel could truthfully claim is struck.

Sheet D, why switch, use alongside, or adopt first: switch defaults to "no brand replaces a supported programme in 2027"; alongside is a feed of people outside the brand's programme and CRM; first is a brand with no programme or a member with no brand. Write "doing nothing" (say the name; send the link) honestly.
Sheet E, what might be hard to copy: each note ends "because" and names a test. Density in one node is a HYPOTHESIS.

Tori closes by reading aloud the one job, for whom, the comparison set (consumer side ShopMy, LTK, Linktree or Beacons, WhatsApp; brand side Duel, Mention Me, impact.com, Extole, Talkable, doing nothing) and the claims the prototype can show.
Write the "who owns the advocate" paragraph: identity, consent, export, and what a brand keeps when a contract ends. Blake writes the product half, Tori the commercial half.

Claims table v1 from sheets C, D and E: claim; versus whom; demonstrable Sunday?; evidence label; hard to copy because. Claims about alternatives cite a URL or a founder's test note and say "not found publicly". "Better" is struck.
Write the Q5 answer block under 150 words; Blake logs D1-04-Q5 with Tori's originator view verbatim.

prompts: What does a Sway page give a recipient that an LTK List over WhatsApp does not?
Duel already says the lever is "the people who already love you". What do we believe that it does not?
Public information only: why is our Trust Map different from an incumbent's intelligence graph?
Who owns the advocate when a brand's contract ends? Write the contract paragraph.
List the data we hold on day ninety; cross out what an incumbent could get. Moat, feature, or report?
If a brand says "send me the list and I will invite them", do we say yes, at what price?
